sections.html:
Gainesville is Alachua County's seat and largest city, a university-driven hub for north central Florida on the I-75 corridor, roughly halfway between Atlanta and Miami. Owners typically pick one of three routes: list with an agent, line up a buyer themselves, or take a cash purchase.

  • Agent: the biggest audience, but showings and buyer loans to manage.
  • Direct: you set the price and sign every form.
  • Cash: few conditions, flexible timing and a price that discounts for repairs.

Judge each bid by what you net after payoffs, tax and recording, and get every offer on paper. If a buyer wants a deposit from you, early transfer of title or an up-front fee, show the paper to an attorney first.

The University of Florida was chosen for Gainesville in 1905, and the city's character has followed the campus ever since. Population is 151,275, median age is 26.4 and median household income is $43,783. Demand for houses tends to follow the academic calendar, and investors weigh rent against price, with plenty of campus-area rental stock in the mix.

The housing itself is varied: older frame houses near downtown, postwar neighborhoods and newer subdivisions toward the I-75 malls. Neighborhoods such as the Duckpond, the southeast and Pleasant Street became historic districts in the 1980s to protect their Victorian homes, and houses close to restored blocks are often the ones carrying historic-district rules.

The city has five local historic districts protecting more than 1,500 historic structures, plus 10 buildings listed individually on the Local Register. Alterations and additions on those properties follow the city's Rehabilitation and Design Guidelines, and an application for a Certificate of Appropriateness begins with a pre-application conference with the Historic Preservation Planner.

Ask that planner whether your house is covered. If it is, say so in your first buyer conversation, since it limits renovation plans, and hand over any Certificate of Appropriateness paperwork you have.

A complete folder shortens the path to the closing table and gives a buyer fewer reasons to renegotiate.

  • Documents showing who can sign: the deed, trust papers or a probate order.
  • Written payoffs for every mortgage, lien or judgment on file in Alachua County.
  • Lease copies, deposit records and rent history for any tenant.
  • Repair and permit records for roof, plumbing, electrical and air conditioning.
  • Your latest tax bill and TRIM notice.
  • Certificate of Appropriateness paperwork when the property is in a historic district.

Florida requires two witnesses to a deed under s. 689.01, so plan a signing with your title agent, a notary and the witnesses present. Get your estimated costs and net in writing before committing.

sections.h2: A house with a renter inside
sections.html: An occupied house attracts a different crowd than an empty one. Investors ask for lease end dates, rent amounts and maintenance history. Section 83.57 governs month-to-month tenancy: the landlord's notice must come 30 or more days ahead of the end of the period. A written lease usually stays in force for the next owner. Decide whether you will hand over keys at closing or transfer the tenancy, and tell every prospective buyer which it is.

The city adopted a Rental Housing Ordinance on September 17, 2020, setting annual permits, inspections and property standards for residential rentals. The city now reports that the ordinance is being repealed and that no specific rental regulations apply at present, although rentals must still meet other city codes.

  • Rentals under 30 days: the city has not regulated them since October 1, 2021.
  • Longer rentals: property maintenance and code enforcement rules still apply.

Ask city Sustainable Development staff for the current status before you describe the rule to a buyer, and ask whether an old landlord permit needs to be closed.

Doc stamps on a Gainesville deed come to 70 cents per hundred dollars of price. The Alachua County clerk takes payment at the counter, and everyone who signs shares liability regardless of what the contract says. Recording fees under s. 28.24 are charged page by page, with trust fund and technology add-ons. Have the title agent print the full total on your closing statement before you sign.

Taxes follow a fixed yearly rhythm, and a closing agent prorates the year's bill at settlement. The tax collector can state the balance.

Yearly tax dates for an Alachua County owner
WhenWhat happens
January 1Assessment date
March 1Homestead filings due
AugustProposed-tax notice arrives
NovemberBills arrive with a 4 percent discount, shrinking a point each month to February
April 1Unpaid taxes delinquent

A sale resets the buyer's assessed value to market the next January. The homestead exemption is up to $50,000.

Florida statutes lay out the sequence in each case. Smaller or older estates may qualify for summary administration under s. 735.201, and s. 733.702 sets a creditor filing cutoff. After a foreclosure judgment, the clerk sells the property at auction on the schedule in s. 45.031. Selling beforehand can preserve equity that an auction may not. An attorney who handles probate or foreclosure can explain your options.

After you accept a written offer, a title company opens a file and searches the Alachua County record for liens, judgments and unpaid taxes. Anything it finds has to be cleared or paid from your proceeds. You then sign the contract, and at closing sign the deed with two witnesses. The agent pays off your lender, collects the stamp tax and recording fees, and sends you the balance. Because no buyer's lender is involved, nobody orders an appraisal, and the buyer is not waiting on underwriting. That is where the speed comes from.

Ask the buyer to say in writing when closing will happen, who pays which cost, and what happens to items left in the house.

A listing may bring a higher price, but it asks for patience: showings, inspection requests, a buyer's loan and weeks of carrying costs. A cash buyer offers speed and certainty, and takes the repairs off your hands, so the price reflects that work. A house with a new roof and a flexible date can do well on the market. One with deferred maintenance, a tenant or a lender's deadline often fits a direct sale better.

Whichever route you favor, get at least two written offers and compare them by net proceeds, not by the number on top.

At closing the title agent reviews the settlement statement with you. Read each line, ask about any charge you do not recognize and confirm that payoffs match your letters. Once the deed is signed and recorded, hand over keys and remotes, and your proceeds arrive by wire or check. Afterward, update your mailing address with the property appraiser and keep copies of everything you signed, including the final settlement statement.

faqs.a: The city covers about 65.27 square miles and has a population of 151,275 from the 2025 BEBR update. Its median age is 26.4.
The city has not regulated rentals of fewer than 30 days since October 1, 2021. County and state rules are separate.

faqs.q: Who can tell me if my Gainesville house is historic?
faqs.a: The city's Historic Preservation Planner can. Gainesville has five local historic districts covering more than 1,500 structures, with extra rules for work on them.

faqs.q: Who pays documentary stamps on a Gainesville sale?
faqs.a: The contract usually assigns it, yet all parties to the deed are liable under the statute. The clerk takes payment at recording.

faqs.q: When do Alachua County taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. November bills carry the largest early-payment discount, and it fades by February.
